preamble: The velar nasal [ŋ] shifting to the bilabial nasal [m] is a change of place from velar to labial. The clearest historical case is Eastern Romance, where Latin ⟨gn⟩, pronounced [ŋn], became [mn]: Romanian lignum > lemn 'wood', signum > semn 'sign', cognatus > cumnat 'brother-in-law', with Aromanian lemnu and semnu and Dalmatian comnut. A present-day case is Hong Kong Cantonese, where younger speakers pronounce the syllabic nasal [ŋ̍] as [m̩], so that 五 'five' and 吳 (a surname) sound like 唔 m.

examples.note: Latin ⟨gn⟩ stood for [ŋn]; in Romanian the velar nasal became bilabial before /n/.
Dalmatian comnut shows the same outcome.
Syllabic velar nasal merged with syllabic /m/ among younger Hong Kong speakers; one of the 'lazy sounds' (懶音).
